title: How many have you installed?
header_line: My analysis of one book on an entrepreneur's life. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: Have you done, with your own hands, the work you give to others?

A student said: a lot of repeating themes from the last chapter. You get to see the culture in action: a person drives six hours, misses his flight, the founder tells him to change everything, and he responds enthusiastically: yes. You can see the type of personnel and their buying into the culture.
I asked: what triggered the surge? For people who don't know, the surge is where he sets impossible deadlines and creates momentum in the company to do the impossible.
A student said it came from pressure to prove the doubters wrong about a business purchase, which then eased on the engineers at the end of the chapter.

One thing that stood out, I said, is that he is adamant about engineers who don't understand the practicality of something. He questions every requirement, and he says: we need engineers out here to see how hard this is to install.

The engineer made the mistake of sounding both assured and condescending: I've got twenty years of experience in the roof business. The founder asked: how many roofs have you installed? He said: I've never installed one. He went ballistic: you're the engineer and you leave this problem to somebody else.
That really sets him off, I said. He is in tune with the process and the design and manufacturing, the A to Z, making sure there is nothing inefficient and not allowing any assumptions to take over.
What have you not tried yourself that you ask your team to do?

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write one task you ask others to do that you have never done.
Write what you would learn by doing it once.
Write a requirement you could question.
Write an assumption in your process.
Write when you will do it yourself.

check.q: What did the founder ask the engineer who sounded assured?
choices: How many roofs have you installed?

check.q: What did I say the person doesn't allow in a process?
What did a student say you can see in the chapter?

recap: Do the work once yourself. Question the requirements. Don't let assumptions run the process.
